<b>Один признак — цвет горошины.</b> Ген: One trait — pea color. A gene comes in variants — alleles: A (yellow) is dominant, a (green) is recessive. Each plant has two copies of the gene; a gamete (after meiosis) gets one. All F1 hybrids (Aa) are yellow, yet in the second generation green returns in a quarter: 3 : 1.
<b>Два признака сразу</b> — цвет (Y/y) и: Two traits at once — color (Y/y) and shape (R/r — round or wrinkled). Genes on different chromosomes separate in meiosis independently, so the YyRr hybrid makes 4 kinds of gametes equally, and the second generation shows 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. Genes lying close on one chromosome are inherited together (linked) unless crossing over separates them.
<b>Группы крови AB0.</b> У гена три алле: ABO blood groups. The gene has three alleles: I^A, I^B and i (group O). I^A and I^B are codominant — a carrier of both has group AB with both antigens on the red cells; i is recessive. So parents with A and B can have children of any of the four groups, and two A parents can have a child with group O.
<b>Наследование, сцепленное с полом.</b>: Sex-linked inheritance. The color-vision gene lies on the X chromosome. Women have two X’s, and the normal allele usually masks the faulty one — she is only a carrier. Men have one X (XY), so colorblindness is ≈ 10–15 times more common in them. A son gets his X only from his mother.
Почему у кареглазых родителей бывает гол: Why can brown-eyed parents have a blue-eyed child, and why is colorblindness more common in men? The monk Gregor Mendel worked it out on peas before DNA was discovered.

Mendel’s laws (1865)

  • Uniformity of F1: crossing pure lines gives identical first-generation hybrids (the dominant trait shows).
  • Segregation: in the second generation 3 : 1 by phenotype and 1 : 2 : 1 by genotype — because alleles go to different gametes (meiosis, anaphase I).
  • Independent assortment of genes on different chromosomes — 9 : 3 : 3 : 1; linked genes are the exception.

In humans

Many traits (height, skin and eye color) depend on many genes and the environment, so they do not split strictly 3 : 1. Mendelian inheritance is seen, for example, in cystic fibrosis and phenylketonuria (recessive), Huntington’s disease (dominant), hemophilia and colorblindness (X-linked).

Terms

Genotype is the set of alleles (AA, Aa, aa), phenotype is how it shows. Homozygous — two identical alleles, heterozygous — different ones. A Punnett square lists all gamete combinations and gives the probabilities.

Conventions

  • Peas, blood-group “drops” and “children” spheres are symbols, not models of cells; sizes are arbitrary.
  • All gametes are taken as equally likely; selection and mutations are ignored; the “100 peas” experiment is a random sample, different every time.
  • Allele symbols are simplified (I^A, I^B, i written as A, B, 0).
